question: When cycling's hour record was reset to traditional bikes in 2000, how far did Chris Boardman ride?
answer: 49.441 km, just 10 metres beyond Eddy Merckx's 49.431 km from 1972. Four years earlier, on a bike built around a stretched-out position with arms forward, Boardman had covered 56.375 km. Nearly seven of those kilometres belonged to the machine and the posture, not to 24 years of human progress.
move: Hold the equipment fixed before you credit the person with the progress.
ask: Which of my improvements came from better tools, and which really came from me?
reference: Chris Boardman, Triumphs and Turbulence: My Autobiography, Ebury Press, 2016
